handoff.output_file: Interactive HTML prototype per persona (responsive .html each), wireframes, interaction flows, visual design prototypes
handoff.handoff_instruction:
Do NOT hand off until UX and UI design have been validated and explicitly approved by the user. Design discovery (aesthetic, visual depth/surface style, theme, responsive strategy, design system, material types: 2D, 3D, animation, etc.) should be completed before handoff; approved prototype reflects user's design preferences (greenfield) or, when brownfield with existing UI, matches existing app's UI components, styles, and look-and-feel pixel by pixel plus any approved enhancements. **If the user explicitly requests a UI change** that requires architecture or plan updates: ensure prototype (create/update) → plan (create/update) run; request return to **architect** only when there is API or architecture impact (new/changed APIs, backend, data model, new modules or integration points). See .nayan/guidance/pipeline-entry-points.md (Explicit UI change requests). **If requirements or architecture need adjustment based on UX findings:** Use new_task with mode=prd (requirements change) or mode=architect (architecture change) and message describing the required changes. Do not proceed to architect or plan until adjustments are made and re-approved.
When approved, validate plan prerequisites (architecture.md, PRD/scope) are ready. Then use new_task with mode=plan and message including: - PRD_FILE: refined-prd.md (greenfield) or SCOPE: condensed scope (brownfield) - ARCHITECTURE_FILE: architecture.md - UX_ARTIFACTS: interactive HTML prototype per persona (paths: ux/prototypes/{persona}/ per persona from PRD Section 5 (greenfield) or condensed scope (brownfield)), wireframes, interaction flows, prototypes (paths or descriptions) - CONTEXT: greenfield|brownfield - TECH_STACK: bootcamp|enterprise|custom - Instruction to synthesize into development-plan.md using the appropriate template, incorporating UX artifacts. **Note:** Approved UX prototype is authoritative for UI design and look-and-feel; development plan and code must implement to match it using the tech stack documented in architecture.md (by architect).
